questions.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{-2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩\cdot ⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩ \\  & ={e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{({e}^{t})}^{2}+{(2{e}^{-2t})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{3},\,{t}^{2}⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩ \\  & =18{t}^{3}+4t \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{18{t}^{3}+4t}{\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,3t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,3⟩\cdot ⟨-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,0⟩ \\  & =64\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\operatorname{cos}⁡4t-64\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\operatorname{sin}⁡4t \\  & =0 \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)}^{2}+{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡4t+16{cos}^{2}⁡4t+9} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡4t+{cos}^{2}⁡4t)+9} \\  & =\sqrt{16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{0}{5} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,\frac{1}{t},\,-1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,0⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}},\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}-\frac{2}{{t}^{5}} \\  & =-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{5}} \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{t})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{5}})}{(\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}{{t}^{2}})} \\  & =-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{3}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+9} \\  & =\sqrt{1+9} \\  & =\sqrt{10}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+9{cos}^{2}⁡t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+1} \\  & =\sqrt{9+1} \\  & =\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{10}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1){e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+2){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\times ⟨(t+2){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ (t+1){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} & 0 \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t} & 0 \\ -{e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} & 0 \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,{e}^{2t}⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{((t+1){e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(t+1)^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{({e}^{2t})}^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{t}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,2t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,2⟩\times ⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨18\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-18\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-27{cos}^{2}⁡3t-27{sin}^{2}⁡3t⟩ \\  & =⟨18\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-18\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-27⟩ \\  & =9⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-3⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡3t+9{sin}^{2}⁡3t+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡3t+{sin}^{2}⁡3t)+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4} \\  & =\sqrt{13}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =9\sqrt{{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3)}^{2}} \\  & =9\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡3t+4{sin}^{2}⁡3t+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡3t+{sin}^{2}⁡3t)+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{4+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{13}} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩\times ⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & {t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2 & 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & {t}^{2} \\ 2 & 2t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,4{t}^{2}-2{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,2{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+({t}^{2})^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+{t}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}(4+{t}^{2})} \\  & =t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}} \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{1}+(0)^{2}+(2{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{4}} \\  & =2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-(t+1){e}^{t},\,2⟩, \\ v(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-(0+1){e}^{0},\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-(t+1){e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-(t+2){e}^{t},\,0⟩, \\ a(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-(0+2){e}^{0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(0)\cdot a(0)$ and $||v(0)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\cdot a(0) & =⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩ \\  & =3, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(0)\cdot a(0)}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

questions.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{2}t,\,t,\,{t}^{3}⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\ v(1) & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,6t⟩ \\ a(1) & =⟨0,\,0,\,6(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\cdot a(1)$ and $||v(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\cdot a(1) & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,6⟩ \\  & =18 \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=1$, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(1)\cdot a(1)}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{18}{2\sqrt{3}} \\  & =3\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $3\sqrt{3}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

questions.problem: The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(0):$

$$
v(0)=⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩, \\ a(0) & =⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(0)\times a(0),||v(0)||,$ and $||v(0)\times a(0)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\times a(0) & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨1,-1,0⟩, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}, \\ ||v(0)\times a(0)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(0)\times a(0)||}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is $1\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

questions.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,t⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=\pi \,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=\pi ,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,1⟩, \\ v(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩, \\ a(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )$ and $||v(\pi )||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi ) & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =0, \\ ||v(\pi )|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )}{||v(\pi )||} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $0\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

questions.problem: The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨-\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2,\,t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s},$ rounded to one decimal place.
questions.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(1):$

$$
v(1)=⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{t},\,0,\,1⟩, \\ a(1) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\times a(1),||v(1)||,$ and $||v(1)\times a(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\times a(1) & =⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩\times ⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2,-1,2⟩, \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{0)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}, \\ ||v(1)\times a(1)|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=1,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(1)\times a(1)||}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & ≈1.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is approximately 
 $1.3\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

canonical_examples.problem: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) =  \langle 1, \, \sqrt{2} t,\, -t^2 \rangle.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,\sqrt{2},\,-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨1,\,\sqrt{2}t,\,-{t}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,\sqrt{2},\,-2t⟩ \\  & =2t+2{t}^{3} \\  & =2t({t}^{2}+1), \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2}t)}^{2}+{(-{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}} \\  & ={t}^{2}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2t({t}^{2}+1)}{{t}^{2}+1} \\  & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t)= \left\langle -4, \, \cos{(2t)},\, \sin{(2t)} \right\rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \times \mathbf a{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨-4,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\times ⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -4 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-4 & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-4 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+2{sin}^{2}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||\mathbf v||$ and $||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(-4)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{16+1} \\  & =\sqrt{17}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+{(8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+64{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64({cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64} \\  & =\sqrt{68} \\  & =2\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{17}}{\sqrt{17}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: The position $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)= \langle e^{2t}, \, e^{-t} , \, 1 \rangle,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t = 0\,\textrm s.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t = 0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{2t},\,-{e}^{-t},\,0⟩, \\ v(0) & =⟨2{e}^{2(0)},\,-{e}^{-0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t = 0{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{e}^{2t},\,{e}^{-t},\,0,⟩ \\ a(0) & =⟨4{e}^{2(0)},\,{e}^{-0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(0) \cdot \mathbf a(0)$ and $||\mathbf v(0)||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\cdot a(0) & =⟨2,\,-1,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨4,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =7, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(0)\cdot a(0)}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\dfrac{7\sqrt{5}}{5} \, \textrm{ms}^{-2}.$
